::: {#rem-devices}

#### Where a tensor lives

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
has_gpu = torch.cuda.is_available()
print(images.device, has_gpu)
```

Every [tensor](#def-tensor) also has a device, the processor whose memory holds it.
PyTorch makes a tensor on the CPU unless told otherwise,
so the [tensors](#def-tensor) on this page live on the `r toupper(py$images$device$type)`.
On a computer with an NVIDIA GPU, which `torch.cuda.is_available()` reports
(it returned `` `r if (py$has_gpu) "True" else "False"` `` on the computer that built this page),
`images.to("cuda")` copies a tensor to the GPU,
where the operations on it then run.
An operation on two tensors needs both on the same device.

:::
